paper: Bosma EF et al. (2016) Complete genome sequence of thermophilic Bacillus smithii type strain DSM 4216^T. Standards in Genomic Sciences 11:52.

open_questions.q: If Bacillus smithii DSM 4216^T lacks pfl, pta, and ackA, what enzymatic route actually generates the observed acetate as the second-most-abundant fermentation product?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md C14 confirms by both name search of the RefSeq annotation and BLASTP (e-value <= 1e-10 against Pta P39646, AckA P37877, PflA P32676, PflB P09373) that none of the three canonical Firmicute acetate-production enzymes are encoded. The paper accepts this as a real gap. But B. smithii still physiologically produces acetate as a second fermentation product (paper statement), so a non-canonical pathway must exist and has not been identified.
next_steps: HMM search of the 3,753 CDS set against Pfam / TIGRFAM families for alternative acetate-forming enzymes: acetyl-CoA synthetase (ACS, PF00501+PF13193), ADP-forming acetyl-CoA synthetase (ACD, archaeal-type), acetate-CoA ligase, phosphoketolase (PF03894), pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR).
Cross-check hits against genome context (co-localisation with pyruvate-node genes) and against expression data if any RNA-seq exists for DSM 4216^T.
Contact the Bosma lab (Wageningen) to ask whether they have subsequent metabolomics / labelled-carbon flux data on DSM 4216^T that isotope-traces acetate origin.

Compare to the closest sequenced sister B. coagulans 2-6 (CP002472.1), which does encode pta/ackA, and to other acetate-producing Firmicutes that lack the classical trio (e.g. certain Clostridium spp. using PFOR + ACD).

open_questions.q: Does the 12,514-bp plasmid replicate by a novel rep family, or is it a defective/integrative element that lacks any autonomous rep gene at all?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md C13: full PlasmidFinder rep-family screen (488 sequences across Inc18, Rep1/2/3, RepA_N, RepL, Rep_trans, NT_Rep) returns 0 hits at default thresholds and only sub-100-bp fragments when relaxed. The paper's own RAST annotation is congruent (all hypothetical protein / mobile element / MazEF, no annotated Rep). Yet the paper reports it as a circular plasmid, implying autonomous maintenance. The replication mechanism is therefore either novel-family or the element is non-autonomous.
next_steps: Re-annotate the 12,514-bp plasmid FASTA with a broader database: full Pfam-A (not just PlasmidFinder), COG, and structural homology via Foldseek against AlphaFold DB.
Look explicitly for HUH-family relaxases (RCR plasmid replication), toprim-domain proteins, or ParA/ParB-only partitioning systems that could indicate an alternative maintenance strategy.

Check whether the plasmid sequence has any near-identical homolog in other Bacillaceae assemblies (BLASTN vs nt) --- a match to an integrative/conjugative element would suggest it is not a true autonomous plasmid.
Long-read raw data (PacBio) from the original submission could confirm true circularity vs a mis-assembled chromosomal region; check SRA for the original raw reads.

open_questions.q: Given ~89-90% ANI between B. smithii DSM 4216^T and both B. coagulans 2-6 and B. subtilis 168 (well below the 95% species boundary), where does B. smithii sit inside a modern GTDB / TYGS classification, and is the current genus assignment still correct?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md C16 shows ANIb-style mean identity of 89.26% vs B. coagulans (its named-closest sister in Table 6) and 89.97% vs B. subtilis. Both are well below the 95% species boundary. The paper predates the Gupta et al. (2020) reorganisation of Bacillus and the elevation of many former Bacillus species into new genera (Alkalihalobacillus, Peribacillus, Cytobacillus, Heyndrickxia, etc.). It is not settled from this replication whether DSM 4216^T should still be called Bacillus smithii.
next_steps: Submit the two accessions to GTDB-Tk classify_wf against the current GTDB release and record the assigned family / genus / species.
Submit to TYGS (Type Strain Genome Server) to get GBDP-based dDDH values against all Bacillaceae type strains.
Cross-reference the LPSN entry for Bacillus smithii to see whether a genus reassignment has already been proposed (Heyndrickxia, Alkalihalobacillus, etc.).
Compute full pyANI ANIm / ANIb (not the fragment approximation used in this replication) against the top 10 GTDB neighbours to get a definitive species-level assignment.

open_questions.q: Is the 8-gene delta in protein-coding count (paper 3,627 vs ours 3,619) and the 8-gene delta in pseudogenes (paper 126 vs ours 134) a real annotation-pipeline shift (RAST vs current RefSeq), or does it reflect a systematic reclassification of specific loci?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md C6 and C8 show a coupled ~8-gene shift: 8 fewer CDS, 8 more pseudogenes. The claims table attributes this to 'RefSeq re-annotation Delta ~6%' but does not identify which specific 8 loci moved. The coupling (same magnitude, opposite direction) is suggestive of a specific set of genes being reclassified as pseudo, but we did not confirm this.
next_steps: Locus-level diff: parse both the original RAST-derived annotation (paper's supplementary table or the initial GenBank submission) and the current RefSeq re-annotation; produce a per-locus comparison table.
Identify the 8 loci that flipped CDS -> pseudo and inspect them (frameshift? in-frame stop? disrupted domain? mobile-element insertion?).
Report whether any of the 8 are functionally significant (e.g. in central carbon metabolism, in the acetate-pathway search space, or in stress-response) as opposed to hypothetical proteins.
This also tightens the C14 negative claim: if any of the 8 reclassified pseudogenes is a truncated pfl/pta/ackA remnant, that would be an important finding beyond the paper's original assertion.

open_questions.q: Are the 69 CRISPR repeats reported in the paper (claim C10, not tested in this replication) still detected by current-generation CRISPR-detection tools, and what is the associated cas gene cassette type?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md C10 is explicitly listed as 'not tested (requires CRT rerun)'. The paper's original 69-repeat call was made with the CRT tool bundled with RAST circa 2015. Current tools (CRISPRCasFinder, CCTyper, CRISPRDetect v3, CasPredict) apply stricter evidence levels and would additionally classify the cas cassette (I-A/I-B/II-C/etc.). For a thermophilic type strain this is not decorative --- CRISPR-Cas type informs both biotech utility and horizontal-transfer resistance.
next_steps: Run CRISPRCasFinder on CP012024.1 and CP012025.1; record evidence-level 4 arrays (the reliable ones) separately from level 1-3.
Run CCTyper on the same to classify the cas cassette type (I / II / III / V / VI subtype).
Compare the current array count and coordinates to the paper's 69 to see whether the delta is (a) evidence-threshold-driven, (b) genuine method drift, or (c) reveals arrays the paper missed.
If a functional cas cassette is confirmed, characterise the spacer set against a phage database (e.g. PHASTER, IMG/VR) to see what phages the strain has historical immunity against.
